title: माध्यमिक तहका मैथिलीभाषी विद्यार्थीहरूले स्तरीय नेपाली  उच्चारणमा गर्ने त्रुटिहरूको अध्ययन{ madhyamik tahaka maithalibhasi bidhyarthile estariy nepali ucharanma garne trutiharuko adhyayan}
nepali: शोधशीर्षक ः “माध्यमिक तहका मैथिलीभाषी विद्यार्थीहरूले स्तरीय नेपाली उच्चारणमा गर्ने त्रुटिहरूको अध्ययन” शोधार्थी ः देवशरण यादव शोधनिर्देशक ः सह–प्रा.महेश्वर न्यौपाने विभाग÷क्याम्पस ः नेपाली भाषा शिक्षा विभाग, विश्वविद्यालय क्याम्पस, कीर्तिपुर शैक्षिक सत्र ः २०६०÷०६२ अध्याय÷पृष्ठ ः अध्याय ५ र पृष्ठ शोधप्रक्रिया प्रस्तुत शोध त्रि.वि.शिक्षाशास्त्र सङ्काय नेपाली भाषा शिक्षा विभागअन्तर्गत एम.एड.दोस्रो वर्ष नेपा.शि.५९८ को आवश्यकता पूर्तिका लागि तयार परिएको हो । विद्यार्थीहरूले स्तरीय नेपाली उच्चारणमा गर्ने त्रुटिहरूको अध्ययनमा केन्द्रित रहेको छ । यसमा सिराहा जिल्लाका ग्रामिण इलाकाका सरकारी र आवसीय मा.वि.लाई समावेश गरिएका छन् । नमुनाका लागि प्रत्येक विद्यालयबाट १०÷१० जना छात्र छात्रहरू छानिएका छन् । ती मध्ये ५÷५ जनाबाट श्रुतिलेखन र ५÷५ जनाबाट उच्चारण गराइएको छ । उच्चारणलाई रेकर्ड पनि गरिएको छ । उनीहरूबाटै स्वतन्त्रलेखन गराउनुको साथै थप औच्चार्यको लागि एउटा अनुच्छेद पढन लगाई त्रुटिहरूको पहिचान गरिएको छ । यसका साथै मा.वि. तहका भाषा पाठ्यपुस्तक, स्थानीय शिक्षक, प्रवुद्धवर्ग र आफ्नो अनुभवबाट १५० वटा सम्भाव्य त्रुटि गर्न सक्ने शब्दहरू छानिएका छन् । नमुनाका लागि छानिएका सबै शब्दहरू प्रत्येक विद्यालयका ५÷५ जना विद्यार्थीहरूबाट उच्चारण गराइएको छ । लेखन र उच्चारणमा कति जनाले कति ठीक र कति गल्ती गरे त्यसको सङ्ख्या गणना गरिएको छ । जसका लागि श्रुतिलेखबाट प्राप्त सामाग्री र उच्चारणको लागि रेकर्ड गरिएको क्यासेट प्रयोग गरिएका छन् । त्यसकै आधारमा सही र गल्तिको प्रतिशताङ्क निकाली तालिकीकरण गरिएको छ । मा.वि.तहका मैथिलीभाषी विद्यार्थीहरू त्रुटि किन र के कति कारणले गर्छन् ? त्यसको चर्चा गरी त्रुटिहरूको व्याख्या विश्लेषण र सामान्य वर्गीकरण गरिएको छ । अन्तमा सबैको निष्कर्ष देखाई त्यस्ता त्रुटिहरू कसरी पन्साउन सकिन्छ त्यसको लागि निराकरणका केही उपायहरू पनि सुझाइएको छ ।
american_english:
Research title: "A Study of the Errors Made by Maithili-Speaking Students at the Secondary Level in Standard Nepali Pronunciation"
Researcher: Devsharan Yadav
Research adviser: Associate Professor Maheshwar Neupane
Department/campus: Department of Nepali Language Education, University Campus, Kirtipur
Academic session: 2060/62 BS
Chapters/pages: 5 chapters and [blank] pages
Research procedure
This study was prepared to satisfy the requirement of Nepa. Shi. 598 in the second year of the M.Ed. program under the Department of Nepali Language Education, Faculty of Education, Tribhuvan University.
It focuses on the study of errors that students make in standard Nepali pronunciation.
Government and residential secondary schools in the rural areas of Siraha district were included in it.
For the sample, 10 boys and 10 girls were selected from each school.
Of them, 5 each were made to do dictation and 5 each were made to pronounce.
Pronunciation was also recorded.
Besides having them do free writing, they were made to read a paragraph for further pronunciation, and errors were identified.
In addition, 150 words that could cause probable errors were chosen from secondary-level language textbooks, local teachers, intellectuals and personal experience.
All the words selected for the sample were pronounced by 5 students from each school.
The number of correct and incorrect responses in writing and pronunciation was counted.
For that, the material obtained from dictation and the cassette recorded for pronunciation were used.
On that basis, the percentage of correct and incorrect responses was worked out and tabulated.
Why and to what extent do Maithili-speaking students at the secondary level make errors? That was discussed, and the errors were explained, analyzed and classified in general terms.
At the end, presenting the conclusions of all of it, some remedies for how such errors can be overcome were also suggested.

Research procedure
The present study was prepared in fulfilment of the requirement of Nepa. Shi. 598 in the second year of the M.Ed. programme within the Department of Nepali Language Education, Faculty of Education, Tribhuvan University.
It is centred upon the investigation of the errors committed by pupils in standard Nepali pronunciation.
Government and residential secondary schools in the rural parts of Siraha district have been included in it.
For the sample, ten boys and ten girls were selected from each school.
Of those, five each were set a dictation and five each were asked to pronounce.
The pronunciation was recorded as well.
Besides being asked to write freely, they were made to read a passage for further pronunciation, and the errors were identified.
In addition, 150 words liable to occasion probable errors were chosen from secondary-level language textbooks, local teachers, learned persons and the researcher's own experience.
Every word chosen for the sample was pronounced by five pupils from each school.
The number of correct and incorrect responses in writing and pronunciation was reckoned.
For this purpose, the material obtained from the dictation and the cassette recorded for pronunciation were employed.
On that very basis, the percentage of correct and incorrect responses was derived and tabulated.
Why, and by how much, do Maithili-speaking pupils at secondary level commit errors? This was discussed, and the errors were explained, analysed and classified in general terms.
Finally, setting out the conclusions of the whole, certain remedies were also suggested for overcoming such errors.
